metadata.file_name: 60. Bozkuş. (2025). Predictors of reading performance of fourth-grade Turkish students.pdf
metadata.title: Predictors of reading performance of fourth-grade Turkish students

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PIRLS 2021 fourth-grade reading data for Türkiye and constructs an analytic dataset by merging questionnaire files into a single R-scripted dataset. The authors report a preprocessing pipeline (purging cases with >20% missingness, then imputing remaining missing values via k-nearest-neighbor mean imputation with k=10, followed by centering and variance scaling) and then manually reduce predictors from 545 to 405. The manuscript does not report applying PIRLS sampling weights or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in the SVM training or evaluation, and the ML workflow (SVM with caret, RFE, repeated k-fold CV, and a 70/30 train-test split) is described without any weight-aware estimation. Given that SVM does not natively incorporate complex survey weights, the analysis appears to proceed as an unweighted ML classification on the prepared sample, which may limit population-representativeness under PIRLS’s clustered sampling design.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PIRLS 2021 openly accessible microdata for Türkiye and restricted to fourth-grade students. The consolidated raw file initially contained 6032 students; cases with more than 20% missing data were removed, reducing the sample to 5538. Remaining missing values were imputed using k-nearest neighbor mean imputation (k=10), and then the dependent variable was recoded into a binary high/low performance identifier using ASRIBM01 (first plausible value benchmark score categories recoded to low vs high). The final analytic dataset for ML contained 3589 students and 405 retained independent variables.

main_findings.target_variable: Reading performance (binary high vs low using ASRIBM01 first plausible value benchmark)
main_findings.performance_metrics: SVM (linear kernel, L2-regularized) — Accuracy: 0.957 (95% CI: 0.943–0.968); Kappa: 0.914; P-value [Acc > NIR] < 0.001; Sensitivity: 0.956; Specificity: 0.958; PPV: ~0.956; NPV: ~0.958; Balanced Accuracy: 0.9572. Feature selection via RFE evaluated subsets of 4, 8, and 16 factors; best top-16 subset reported as improving performance relative to smaller subsets (full 405-variable model: RMSE 0.2618, R² 0.72766, MAE 0.2131; 16-variable subset: RMSE 0.4784, R² 0.08714, MAE 0.4546).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PIRLS 2021 Grade 4 Reading (Türkiye) the study leveraged school emphasis on foundational literacy (letter-sound and alphabet knowledge, reading words) together with teacher assessment and instructional practices (observing students, short written assessments, text-evidence prompts) to predict reading performance as a binary high-vs-low outcome, finding that the SVM achieved 0.957 accuracy with Kappa=0.914 and balanced accuracy=0.9572. This indicates that strengthening school-level instructional emphasis on early decoding/word reading and adopting interactive, evidence-based assessment and teaching practices—alongside supportive parental readiness engagement—may improve the proportion of students reaching higher reading performance benchmarks, though the results are predictive and not causal.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PIRLS 2021 fourth-grade reading data for Türkiye, recoding the dependent variable into a binary high vs low reading performance indicator using ASRIBM01 from the first plausible value benchmark categories. After preprocessing (removing cases with >20% missingness, imputing remaining missing values with k-nearest neighbor mean imputation using k=10, and normalizing), the authors train an L2-regularized linear-kernel SVM in caret with a 70/30 train-test split (n=2513 train; n=1076 test) and use 5-times repeated 10-fold cross-validation for model evaluation and recursive feature elimination (RFE) to identify the most influential predictors. The best model reports Accuracy=0.957 (95% CI 0.943–0.968), Kappa=0.914, sensitivity=0.956, specificity=0.958, and balanced accuracy=0.9572, with P<0.001 versus the no-information rate. The top predictors emphasize school instructional emphasis on foundational literacy and teacher assessment/interactive comprehension strategies, plus parental commitment to readiness. Limitations include the lack of reported complex-survey weight usage and the cross-sectional, predictive nature of the classification (no causal identification).
